key_insight: A mesh-free deep energy method predicts thermally driven crack nucleation, spacing, propagation and arrest without prescribing crack paths or nucleation sites.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support thermal-shock assessment of brittle components with evolving temperature gradients and initially unknown fracture patterns.
method: Use separate multiresolution neural networks for displacement–phase fields and transient temperature.
Minimize mechanical energy and a backward Euler thermal functional using integration points resampled each iteration.
Restrict irreversibility to the crack set, retain optimizer state across load steps and decay learning rates within each step.
evidence_signal: Tests show close agreement with finite element initiation peak loads on two notched plates, an oscillation threshold near linear stability predictions in quenched glass, and ceramic-slab crack spacing near a published benchmark.
watch_item: Slab and annulus crack arrays are denser than finite element predictions on the same material field, leaving crack-density agreement unresolved.
paper_title: A mesh-free deep energy method for phase-field modeling of thermally driven brittle fracture
